Commentary.Commentary: So, a little over two days to go and 188 overs to be bowled, the task for the visitors is clear. They need to be firm and resolute in their approach, something they have failed to prove in the tour so far. If they go for their shots in conducive conditions for pace bowling, they will be going downhill pretty soon. The on-air commentators inform that there are chances of rain around on Day 4 and Day 5. So, it is a game of patience now. New Zealand are favourites to take the series 2-0. Let's find out what happens.

Miguel Cummins was the pick of the bowlers and he bowled his heart out on a track that has juiced up. Got rewarded with three wickets as well. Shannon Gabriel was also brilliant with the ball and took two wickets but the issue of no balls haunted him once again.

After conceding a lead of 152, the Windies picked up two quick wickets but a timely counter-punch from the hosts kept them ahead of the 8-ball. Williamson scored a free-flowing fifty to give good company to Taylor and the latter was ably allied by the lower order as well.

Kane Williamson decides that 443 on the board is enough and SIGNALS FOR THE DECLARATION. A brilliant batting effort from Ross Taylor has powered the hosts to a dominant total. He was not shy to play his shots and went on to score his 17th Test century equaling Kane Williamson and Martin Crowe.
Shorter in length, Taylor hangs back and stonewalls it.
Tossed up delivery, Taylor lunges forward in defense.
Simon Doull on air informs that there might be a declaration around the corner.
Uses his feet and blocks this one.
Southee hangs deep in the crease and turns it towards backward square leg.
Another short delivery, Rosco sits underneath it.
Well-directed bouncer on off, ducked under comfortably.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. They pick up a single.
Very full, tailing in towards the boots. Southee tries to jam it out but gets an inside edge onto his pads.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Cummins goes short this time. Southee is up for it and pulls it with authority in front of square leg and the ball whistles away to the fence. Southee is one of the best strikers of the cricket ball lower down the order says Simon Doull on air.
FOUR! Shouts of catch it but a boundary results! Full length ball, swinging into Southee. He clips it uppishly over mid-wicket and the ball races to the ropes.
Cummins stops in his delivery stride. Probably lost his rhythm on this occasion.
Leans forward to the loopy delivery on middle and works it to short mid-wicket.
Down the leg side, left alone.
FOUR! Well played! On a fullish length outside off, no real turn on offer. Taylor puts his front foot towards the line of the ball and caresses it through the vacant point region for a boundary.
Slow through the air, Taylor prods forward in defense.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Down the leg side, Ross tries to help it with the spin but misses.
Full on leg stump, clipped to the leg side for a single.
Gabriel is back on the field.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Just short of the keeper! Back of a length ball around off, Taylor goes for a pull but gets a bottom edge that just drops in front of he crouching Dowrich.
Back of a length delivery around off, Taylor shuffles across and opts to take it on the body. The ball rolls towards square leg. Rosco has a wide grin on his face.
Sits up nicely for Southee who hammers it to deep mid-wicket to rotate strike.

A stifled appeal for an LBW is turned down. Cummins goes wider of the crease and angles in a full length delivery. Southee looks to play it across but is pinged on the pads. A shout follows but the umpire stays put. Replays show that it was going down leg.
Spinning down the leg side, Taylor pads it away. The ball goes past the keeper and rolls to the fence behind. Dead ball signaled by the umpire as no shot was offered to that.
Around the pads, Taylor looks to clip it away but gets hit on the pads.
Fullish on middle, turned with the spin to square leg.
Leans forward and taps it to cover-point for a swift single.
On middle and leg, spinning down. Tim aims to whip it through but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
On a flatter trajectory, Southee hangs back and defends it solidly.
Trent Boult is padded up. Seems like New Zealand are going to bat on.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, kept out watchfully.
On a length on middle, pushed past the bowler towards mid on.
Slower delivery, actually really slow for a pace bowler at 102.1 clicks. Southee pats it past the diving Reifer and scurries across to the other end.
FOUR! Heaved away! Fullish delivery on off, Southee clears his front leg and drags it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Short and room on offer, cut away to sweeper cover for a single.
FOUR! Shot! Outside off and spinning in, Southee hangs back and cuts it against the spin through point to find the fence. New Zealand lead by 420 now.
Fullish delivery, eased off the front foot to mid on.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Drifting away with the arm, Southee shapes for the cut but gets beaten.
Waits for this one to turn into him and nudges it to mid-wicket.
Slow through the air on middle and leg, Southee tries to play it across but gets a soft leading edge down the track.
Back of a length ball on leg stump, pushed off the back foot to mid on.
Full length delivery on middle, patted back to the bowler.
The batsman has played the square drive. One run added to the total.
Short delivery on middle and leg, bludgeoned to deep square leg to rotate strike.
Hangs back to the good length delivery and blocks it with a straight bat.
No ball. Full delivery outside off, driven crisply to covers. Alas, a West Indian bowler has overstepped again.

FOUR! 17th Test century for Ross Taylor! He equals Kane Williamson and Martin Crowe's record. Well played Rosco. Fractionally overpitched around off, Taylor drives it elegantly through mid off to find the fence. Lifts his bat towards the dressing room and sinks in all the applause. Is the declaration coming soon?
Birthday boy, Tim Southee, walks out to bat now. He will be aiming to make this day memorable when he gets the ball in his hand later on...

DRINKS BREAK. Nothing much left in this innings apart from Taylor's century. He has played fluently and will look to get it as soon as possible. One thing which will interest the Kiwis is the length Gabriel has been bowling. His wickets have come from a length and a certain Neil Wagner will be keenly observing that spot. 22 overs left in the day. How many does Williamson plan to give the Windies?

OUT! Straight to the man! Short and outside off, Wagner gives this the kitchen sink but finds the man at point. Shai Hope takes it just above the ground. Wagner walks back a bit disappointed. New Zealand are effectively 409/8 but that does not matter. All eyes are on whether Taylor can get to a century.
Full again, watchfully kept out.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, defended from the crease.
Full on middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single to move to 96.
On middle, pushed towards mid on.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

On the pads, flicked towards short mid-wicket. Taylor goes for the quick single and the fielder has a shy at the bowler's end. Hits the stumps and there is an appeal for a run out but Tucker shakes his head. Taylor was comfortably in.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single.
RAYMON REIFER is given the ball now. Cummins was a bit unhappy in that last over and was seen struggling.
Outside off, pushed towards cover.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full and outside off, pushed towards short extra cover.
Slower through the air, full and around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, a bit of flight, pushed past cover for a single. Wagner comes back for the second but is sent back.
Full and on the pads, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a couple.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single.
A bouncer now, Taylor ducks.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
A length ball, on middle, Rosco looks to work it to the leg side but misses. The ball pops off his pads and lands near where short leg would have been. Was there an inside edge? Not sure.

FOUR! But a bit streaky. Banged in short, outside off, Taylor goes for the pull but miscues it. The ball goes off the top edge but it is well wide of Roston Chase running to his left at the mid-wicket fence. Into the 90s goes Taylor. THE LEAD CROSSES 400.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, well blocked out.
Outside off, pushed through to mid off for a single.
Full on middle, pushed straight to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

FOUR! Good shot. Not a bad ball, banged in short and angling away from the body, Wagner gets on top of the bounce and punches it past point for a boundary. Flashes his teeth as he walks towards Taylor. That sign always comes on every bowler's face when he gets a boundary.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A bouncer now, on middle, Neil ducks.
Fuller, driven straight to mid off.
A good length ball on middle, defended watchfully.
Simon Doull on air informs us that he has just been informed that Kemar Roach has a back problem. So, in all likelihood, he may not bowl now. MIGUEL CUMMINS is back on.
Gets off the mark with a nudge through the leg side for a single.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Shannon Gabriel is walking off the field. Looks like he is done for the day and for the match as well.
Outside off, pushed through mid off for a single.
Full on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
A length ball on middle, Wagner looks to play straight but is comprehensively beaten as he plays inside the line.
Short and outside off, Rosco flashes hard and gets a thick outside edge. Lands in front of Shai Hope who is not able to stop it cleanly. A single taken. The lead is now worth 390.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to mid off.
Very full, almost sneaks beneath the bat, Taylor jams it out towards mid on.
On a length around off, solidly defended.
Full and straight, well kept out.
On middle, gently tapped to the leg side.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Outside off, Wagner gets a good stride forward and then lets it go.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, Taylor pushes at this away from his body and gets a thick outside edge to third man. Takes a single. 16 more runs... the Windies will be hoping.
Defends this solidly.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
NO BALL NUMBER 15 in the match for Gabriel. A bouncer, down the leg side. Wagner ducks.
A length ball on middle, defended back to the bowler.
NEIL WAGNER is in at number 9, replacing Blundell.

OUT! Edged and taken! Gabriel gets his second. He has bowled his heart out in this spell. Bends his back, lands it exactly on that spot which is causing problems to the batsmen - the length. The ball moves off the seam and it is actually a tentative poke from Blundell. Perhaps he wanted to leave that but had already committed too far. As a result, ended up giving catching practice to Kieran Powell at first slip. NEW ZEALAND EFFECTIVELY 387/7.
Short and outside off, cut away for a single.
Down the leg side, Taylor misses his flick and is hit on the pads.

FOUR OVERTHROWS! Looks like a bunch of Santas is on the field. Windies at their generous best. Taylor flicks it towards fine leg and jogs across for an easy single. The fielder picks the ball and returns a wild throw to the keeper who misses it. One plus four equals 5. The stand is worth 22 from 21 balls now. Taylor moves to 82. Can't help but feel that the Windies want Taylor to get to his 100 quickly and then declare.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
FOUR! More bad bowling, short and down the leg side, Taylor rocks back and pulls it past short fine leg and gets another boundary. The lead moves to 381.
Pushes this past the bowler and eventually gets off the mark with a single.
Good bowling, full on middle, chipped uppishly back to the bowler. Nearly carried.
Tossed up on middle, Blundell comes down the track and flicks it straight to short mid-wicket.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Now he troubles Taylor. The ball pitching on a length seems to be causing the trouble. Neither full nor short. It is jagging off the seam and making life difficult for the ones who have the willow. Taylor looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
One more ball jagging back in but it is down the leg side. Blundell cannot get it away but manages to get off strike as the ball deflects off his pads to the leg side. A leg bye signalled.
Fuller, but outside off, Tom shoulders arms. And... it is NO BALL NUMBER 7 for Gabriel.
How did that miss the stumps? Gabriel bowls a peach, pitching this on a length and then making it dart back off the seam, cutting Blundell into half and just making the ball go over the stumps!
Clips it through the leg side and takes a single.
FOUR! Full and wide outside off, Taylor throws his bat at it and gets a thick outside edge, just past gully to the third man fence. Moves to 72 and the lead is now 373.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
Full and on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Closer to the stumps, pushed through point for a single.
FOUR! Another gift. Short and down the leg side. Taylor pulls it past short fine leg and gets a boundary. Rank bad delivery.
Full again, on the pads once more, flicked straight to short fine leg.
Full and down the leg side, Taylor misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
Driven through the covers by the batsman. A committed effort by the fielder to save runs for his team.
On middle and off, watchfully defended.
TOM BLUNDELL is the new man in, at number 8, replacing de Grandhomme.

OUT! Decision reversed but what happened there? Umpire Ian Gould gave his decision as not out initially, then changed it to out! Poor Rod Tucker looks confused. Bizarre. Probably the first good ball of the session. Gabriel lands this on a length and gets it to jag back in. De Grandhomme is caught in his crease as he looks to defend but he is hit high on the pads, that too, with his feet up in the air. Gabriel appeals but umpire Tucker says no. Brathwaite has a chat with his bowler and then signals for the review. Now here is where the goof-up happens. Umpire Ian Gould checks the Snickometer time and again and he feels there is an inside edge. Or does he? First, he is not sure. Then, he reckons that the batsman has hit it. So, he asks Tucker to stay with the decision. NOT OUT is the signal. Then suddenly, he checks for the Hawk Eye and that shows the ball to be hitting the stumps! Now, because Hawk Eye is showing that, Gould asks Tucker to reverse his decision! So de Grandhomme has to walk back. Now, if this is the right decision made, was the right protocol followed? First, the third umpire is not sure whether the batsman has hit it. Then he says, there is an inside edge. If you feel there is an inside edge why go for the Hawk Eye? Anyways, de Grandhomme has to walk back and Gabriel has his first wicket of the innings. New Zealand are effectively 364/6.
Howzzat? De Grandhomme is pinged on the pads and Gabriel appeals but umpire Tucker shakes his head. Gabriel wants it reviewed and Kraigg Brathwaite agrees. Height seems to be an issue.

FOUR! Free flow of runs now. A half volley, totally misdirected, on the pads and de Grandhomme just gives it direction towards the fine leg fence. The 50-run stand is up in just 68 balls. De Grandhomme moves to 22 from 30 balls.
Flicks this straight to short mid-wicket.
Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a single. The lead is now worth 360.
FOUR! Freebie for de Grandhomme. Short and wide outside off, Colin just steers it behind point and beats the man rushing to his left.
Comes down the track and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and in line of the sticks, watchfully kept out.
Works this straight to short mid-wicket again.
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, de Grandhomme pushes this back to the bowler who deflects it to extra cover instead. What should have been a dot becomes a single.
ROSTON CHASE to bowl from the other end.
Full and outside off, pushed towards the bowler.
Full on middle, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.

FIVE NO BALLS! Absolute gift. Santa Gabriel is back in town. First he oversteps which is must in every spell of his. 6th no ball in his 11th over. Then, he bowls a bouncer which is way, way high. Would have been wided had it not been for the no ball. De Grandhomme ducks but not sure he needed to. Poor Dowrich leaps full stretch but the ball is miles over his glove as well. Straight to the fence behind. Christmas has come early as the Kiwi 200 is raised. The lead crosses 350 as well.
Around middle, shoots off the pitch, chipped towards mid on.
Slightly short, tapped towards cover for a single.
FOUR! BEAUTY! Gabriel bowls this a bit more fuller and Taylor is ready. Comes forward and drives it wide of cover for a boundary! Moves to 60 with his 5th boundary. The stand moves to 33 as well.
A length ball on middle, pushed towards short mid-wicket.

The players walk out to the middle. In the background, Kane Williamson and Jason Holder are seen chatting with each other. Good to see that - skippers sharing notes. SHANNON GABRIEL to start off the final session to Ross Taylor. Here we go...
Welcome back for the last session of Day 3. All of a sudden, from nowhere, a bunch of dark clouds have accumulated near the ground. It has grown tremendously overcast but we should start on time.
... DAY 3, FINAL SESSION ...

What now for New Zealand? Bat on for as long as possible? There is plenty of time in this Test match but doubt they will play for more than 20 overs. They will love to have a crack at the Windies tonight itself. 38 overs left in the day. So another 100 runs might be the plan. Join us back at 1530 LOCAL (0300 GMT) for the final session.

Miguel Cummins was bowling with fire after Lunch, getting Williamson and Nicholls with terrific deliveries. He had Taylor and Santner in trouble too but both were dropped. Then, the Windies became flat and the duo pounced. Santner was eventually dismissed but at 111/4, the Kiwis were looking in some trouble.

Mixed session. The Windies picked up 2/15 in the first 4 overs but since then have conceded 79 in 23 overs for just the scalp of Santner. There were signs of a possible Kiwi collapse but Taylor has cancelled that.
Around off and middle, solidly defended. TEA ON DAY 3, NEW ZEALAND LEAD BY 342!
Full on middle, hint of inswing, flicked straight to mid on.
Goes back in his crease and blocks.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, Taylor pushes this through the covers. Should have been just a single but Gabriel fumbles. Taylor wants the second but then changes his mind. So eventually, it is just a single.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads for a single.
Full on middle, pushed straight to mid on.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off, cut behind point for a boundary. Cummins is frustrated. He expected sweeper cover to cut that off. The lead is now 340.
Fuller in length, watchfully blocked out.
Around off and middle, defended from the crease.
On middle, defended solidly.
Comes down the track and eases it through covers for a single. Brings up his 29TH TEST FIFTY, steering his team out of somewhat troubled waters.
Full on middle, driven straight back.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On middle and leg, clipped to square leg.
On middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full on middle, pushed towards the bowler.
Another flick, another run.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads for a single.
Goes right back in his crease and blocks.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Appeal for LBW, turned down. Inside edge, as de Grandhomme looks to flick.
Around off, defended watchfully.
MIGUEL CUMMINS into the attack now.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
On middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.

FOUR! Pitiable effort from Gabriel. Outside off, Taylor goes back and cuts this at the last possible moment, almost from the gloves of the keeper towards third man. Should have been only a couple but Gabriel at the ropes jogs across lazily to his left, sticks out his boot but just misses the ball. The stand moves to 20 and the lead is triple Nelson.
On middle, flicked away for a run.
Full and outside off, pushed to long off for a single.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
Similar ball, CdG looks to drive again and mistimes it to cover.
Very full and wide outside off, Colin looks to drive but misses.

SIX! Effortless! That is the power of this man. Fractionally short in length around off, de Grandhomme swivels across and just plays a short-arm jab. Goes all the way over square leg! Moves to 10 and takes the partnership to 14.

Schoolboy stuff. The fielding has not been great from the Windies today, to be polite. Full and outside off, de Grandhomme drives it through the covers for what should have been only a single. But Sunil Ambris comes charging in and in his excitement to do a quick pickup and throw, misses the ball completely. Another run added to the total. The lead is now 321.
A length ball outside off, angling in, watchfully defended to cover.
Outside off, cut through point for a single. Unless my eyes are deceiving me, that fielder was Shannon Gabriel. He is back on the field then.
On the pads this time, flicked straight to mid-wicket.
Bowls this faster, on off, de Grandhomme gets across and bunts it back to the bowler.
Faster on middle, watchfully defended.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads for a single.
Works this straight to short mid-wicket.
Short again, cut again, this time only for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

OVERTHROW. Short and wide outside off, Taylor cuts it behind point and takes a single. The fielder is not happy with that and gets more generous. Returns a wild sloppy throw over the keeper's head and the batsmen take the second. Taylor moves to 41.
Off the mark. Poor bowling again, wide outside off, eased through point for a single.
More filth, wide outside off to a newcomer, not played at.
Wide outside off, left alone.
Down the leg side, flicked straight to short fine leg.
Outside off, pushed towards cover now.
A bit flat, tucked towards short mid-wicket again.
Full on middle, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
COLIN DE GRANDHOMME walks in at number 7, replacing Santner.

OUT! Caught at long on! First wicket for a spinner in this game. Flighted a touch, around middle, Santner comes down the track looking to go big but is not quite to the pitch of the ball. Also, the ball is delivered slightly slower which induces a stroke played a bit early by Santner. The change in pace brings about some turn as well and all these factors result in a miscue. Sunil Ambris comes running in from long on to his right and takes it calmly. The stand is broken as soon as it touches 50.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, holds off the pitch, Taylor comes forward and pushes it uppishly towards the bowler.
This one comes in as well, much closer to the off pole, RT defends it confidently.
Outside off, coming in, shouldered arms to.
Full on middle, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
Bangs it on a length outside off, angles it into Rosco from around the wicket, the batsman hops and defends.
Full again, but closer to the off stump, left alone once more.
MASSIVE WIDE. Fuller in length, bowled almost outside the pitch on the off side. Even if Taylor wanted to, he would not have been able to hit that. The 50-run stand is raised.
With Gabriel off the field, a bowling change is made. RAYMON REIFER to bowl now.
Another quick ball, on the stumps, Mitchell gets his bat down in a hurry to play the ball to the off side.
Quicker, on middle, pushed to short mid-wicket.
Floated outside off, Santner lunges and then leaves it alone.
A tad shorter, on leg stump, Rosco goes back and tucks it wide of backward square leg for a quick single.
On the pads, Taylor comes forward and pushes it towards mid on.
Tossed up on off, pushed back to the bowler.
Gabriel is going off the field due to an injury now.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Full and on middle and off, Santner looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
ANOTHER NO BALL. Number 5 for Gabriel. In his 10th over. This is pushed to mid on for a single. The lead moves to 311.
NO BALL. The customary one in every Gabriel spell. Oversteps again, though not as giant as the previous ones. Just crosses the line. Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Sensible. Leaves the ball alone outside off.
Poorer shot. The length is not even there to cut this time but Rosco is adamant he will play that shot. Does not bother to move his feet either and has a lazy slash. Misses, then smiles.
Almost a reminiscence of his first innings dismissal. Short and outside off, not that wide to cut but Taylor still goes to cut. Extra bounce defeats him. Just past the outside edge.
On a good length on middle, pushed to the leg side.
Faster ball, on off, a forward block to end the over.
Full on middle, flatter though, watchfully defended.

FOUR! Not all that full but plenty of width on the same. Santner reaches out to drive but gets a thick outside edge. Luckily for him, the ball lands in between backward point and point and races to the fence.
More air. This time Mitchell is half forward but drives confidently to cover again.
Comes forward this time on seeing a little bit of flight and pushes the ball to cover.
Full and straight, Santner neither comes forward nor goes back. Just a dead block.

Time for Drinks. New Zealand continue to hold the upper hand and have swelled the lead past the 300-run mark. Two dropped catches even though they were tough has made life even more difficult for the visitors. Can they draw inspiration from somewhere and pull off something heroic? Let's find out... Meanwhile, Roston Chase to roll his arm over now.
Nice end to the over. Gabriel bends his back and bowls an effort ball around off. Taylor moves around gingerly and keeps it off the outer half towards gully.
Slips this one down the leg side, Ross tries to glance it but misses.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, driven with a lot of assurance but straight to the man at covers.

Good fielding, Chase! Bouncer on off, Taylor pulls it hard through mid-wicket. Chase hares to his left, dives full length and stops it. He rolls over the ball but luckily, doesn't parry it to the ropes. Saves a couple of runs for his side.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Dropped! A tough chance goes down. Back of a length delivery outside off, angling in. Taylor doesn't pick up the length and line well and goes for a cut. Ends up getting a fat outside edge that travels a fast pace towards Shai Hope at gully. He crouches to his left, gets both his hands to it but the ball bursts through. The visitors need to take those if they are to comeback into the contest.
Shannon Gabriel returns for a spell.
Back of a length delivery, Santner defends it stoutly.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
In the zone outside off, left alone.
Good length delivery going down the leg side, Santner looks to tuck it away but is hit on the thigh pad.
Back of a length delivery, answered with a straight bat.

FOUR! Santner is growing in confidence. Gets one in the arc outside off and leans forward to cover drive it for a majestic boundary. New Zealand take the lead past the 300-run mark. The all-rounder has shown great courage today after being hit on the helmet. Shows that he is a gutsy character.
No ball! Roach comes from around the wicket and bowls a length ball on off, Santer covers the line and defends it nicely. Roach has overstepped this time.
Finally, Brathwaite takes himself out of the attack. The right move as Kemar Roach to have a burst now.

FOUR! Lucky runs! Well-directed bouncer in line of the stumps, Taylor goes for a forehand pull shot compulsively but ends up getting a top edge. Dowrich leaps full stretch but the ball goes past him in a flash and rockets to the fence.
Half volley outside off, Taylor drills it straight to the fielder at deepish mid off. He has a grin on his face after playing that.
Good length ball outside off, punched firmly off the back foot to covers.
Nervy! Short of a length ball around off, Ross hangs back and pushes at it tentatively but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Once bouncer signaled for the over. Too short, Taylor shapes for the pull but bails out eventually.
Back of a length delivery, defended solidly off the back foot.
The ball has been lost due to the big hit and hence, a replacement is brought in.

SIX! Poor delivery and duly punished! A long hop on off, Santner rocks back and pulls it with aplomb over deep mid-wicket. It is going, going and gone. Huge!! That should be the end of Brathwaite's spell.
Tossed up delivery, Mitchell lunges forward in defense.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Poor fielding! Shortish on middle, Santner punches it back to Brathwaite who makes a meal of it. A run conceded.
Half-tracker on middle and leg, helped past the short fine leg fielder for a run.
Short and room on offer, ample time for Santner to rock back and place it to sweeper cover for an easy single.
Fractionally overpitched around off, driven back to the bowler.
Opts to go short again, comes at a comfortable height to Santner who pushes it past the short leg fielder to rotate strike.
Similar delivery, Santner shows good courage and blocks it stoutly. Cummins probably needs to bowl a full and accurate delivery now to catch him off guard.
Short of a length ball on middle and leg, Mitchell hops and keeps it out nicely.
No ball! Cummins goes for a bouncer as expected. It is too high though and Santner ducks under it.

Oh gosh! Ross Taylor signals for the physio to attend to Santner. That was a hard blow. Hope he is alright. He is taking his time. Seems fine for now. Tough times lie ahead as Cummins will keep bending his back.

Oh no... that's dangerous! Short delivery on middle and leg, Santner doesn't watch the ball and tries to duck under it too quickly. Ends up getting hit on the grille of the helmet. The short leg fielder goes up to him to check whether he is okay or not. The rest of the fielders encircle him.
Shortish delivery on off, Santner hops and blocks it nicely.
Stays leg side of the tossed up delivery and caresses it to sweeper cover for a single.
Strides forward and strokes it to covers.
Santner rocks back and cuts it with the spin to point.
A short delivery which has been pulled away. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Fullish delivery, patted back to the bowler.

The Windies are missing a trick here. The track has quickened up and there is a lot of bounce on offer but Brathwaite continues to bowl. His part-time spinners look pretty bland at the moment. Might be worrying about the slow over-rate and hence, the decision.
On the pads, turned to short fine leg.
Bouncer on middle and leg, pulled hard to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Driven to mid off by the batsman.
Short delivery, Taylor absolutely clubs it but finds the man at mid-wicket.
Overpitched around off, pushed off the front foot to mid off.
Hangs back to the length delivery and blocks it with a straight bat.
FOUR! Hit with disdain! Cummins opts for another bouncer but this time it sits up nicely for Taylor. He stands tall and hammers it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Short ball outside off, placed with the spin to point.
Leans forward and taps it to covers.
Short delivery, cut past point for a single.
Prods forward to this one and blocks it.
Turned with the spin to mid-wicket.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.

FOUR and technically, a dropped chance! This is one amazing spell from Cummins. He runs in hard and puts his all behind this delivery. Gets a lot of extra bounce and gets Santner hopping. The ball brushes his top hand and flies behind. Dowrich leaps like a goalkeeper, gets his right hand on the ball but it deflects behind and rolls to the fence. Brilliant effort though.

Ooh... just short of Shai Hope at gully! Brilliant delivery. Shortish on off, shooting off the deck. Santner gets into an awkward position and ends up gloving it but the ball falls just short of Hope.
Well played. Back of a length ball on off, Santner rises with the bounce and blocks it with a straight bat.
Short cover in place now.
Cummins hit the deck hard, Santner ducks under it in a jiffy.
Bouncer on middle, pulled through square leg for a single.
Fullish delivery, pushed back to the bowler.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Half-tracker outside off, Santner places it past the keeper and the ball rolls to the third man fence.
Steered with the angle through short third man for a run.
Fullish delivery, driven crisply towards mid on where the fielder dives to his left to make a good stop.
Shortish delivery, punched off the back foot to mid-wicket.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Down the leg side, Taylor tries to tuck it away but misses.
Mitchell Santner strides out to bat.

OUT! Cummins is on fire! Fierce spell of fast bowling and he is reaping the dividends. Bangs in another bouncer in line of the stumps, generates appreciable extra bounce on that and also gets it to seam away sharply. Nicholls is caught in a tangle, follows it and ends up getting a faint nick behind. Shane Dowrich moves to his left and accepts it gleefully. The umpires check for the front foot no ball but Cummins is fine. Always a joy to watch when a fast bowler is on song. Good passage of play for the visitors.
Wide! Cummins hit the deck hard but the bouncer is too short. Nicholls ducks under it.
Dug in short on middle, pulled with command to deep mid-wicket to rotate strike.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
That one zipped through! Back of a length delivery on off, some extra bounce on that. Taylor is surprised by that and looks to fend it off but gets hit on the bottom hand.
On a length on middle and leg, kept out watchfully.
Juicy full toss on the pads, helped to deep mid-wicket for a brace. With that, Ross Taylor becomes the first Kiwi batsman to score 1000 runs against the Windies.

Shortish delivery, Nicholls cuts it towards cover-point where the fielder dives to his left to make a half stop. Taylor wants a run but the fielder is quick to recover. Nicholls rightly sends his partner back.
Leans forward to the in drifting delivery and blocks it solidly.
Outside off, skidding after pitching. Nicholls has his stumps covered and makes a good leave.
Going away with the arm, glided to third man for a single.
Taylor is nimble on his feet and pushes it back to the bowler.
Prods forward and blocks the flighted delivery solidly.
Low full toss outside off, Nicholls drives it crisply but finds the man at covers.
The batsman has worked it off his pads behind square. One run added to the total.
Sits deep in the crease and pulls it to the leg side to rotate strike.
FOUR! Sublime timing! Back of a length ball on middle, Nicholls gets on top of the bounce and pulls it through square leg to get off the mark with a boundary.
Length delivery well outside off, left alone.
Henry Nicholls is the new man in.

OUT! Timber! What a scorcher of a delivery to send the set Kiwi skipper packing. Cummins steams in and delivers a pinpoint yorker on off, Williamson falls over a bit to the off side in a bid to jam it out and misses it completely to get the furniture behind him shattered. Always tricky to face a yorker and Williamson was late to react this time. He blinks his eye after getting dismissed. A resourceful knock has come to an end. Second wicket for Cummins. The Windies need to keep chipping away at the wickets.
Miguel Cummins to bowl from the other end.
Sits deep in the crease and works it through square leg for a run. Wants the second but the fielder is quick to attack the ball.
Pushed across the Kiwi skipper who dabs it towards cover-point.
Waits for it and turns it to mid-wicket.
Brathwaite continues to be short, Williamson rocks back and clips it expertly in the gap between the two mid-wicket fielders. The man from wide long on does the mopping up job. A couple taken.
Similar delivery, tucked past the left side of the leg gully fielder for a run.
Starts off with a short delivery on the pads, tucked quietly towards square leg.

We are back to get going again. Kane Williamson and Ross Taylor to continue their innings. The approach from them will be to stay positive and deflate the visiting side further. The weather is holding up so far and we hope that it stays the same way. A nice breeze blowing across the ground at the moment. Kraigg Brathwaite to bowl first up after Lunch. A leg gully in place. Here we go...
... DAY 3, AFTERNOON SESSION ...

Latham also failed to get going and was trapped in front of the stumps by Raymon Reifer. After that, Williamson and Taylor have looked largely at ease stitching a quickfire 50-run stand. Some shoddy fielding from the visitors allowed the duo off the hook. The rhythm of the bowlers also dipped and the hosts have capitalized on it. The Black Caps lead by 248 runs with 8 wickets in hand and a long hard day beckons for the tourists unless they trigger a collapse. Join us shortly for the afternoon session.

New Zealand continue to have a stranglehold on the proceedings. After taking the last two wickets in a jiffy, they have responded nicely with the bat as well. The Windies' bowlers were really disciplined to begin with and persisted with nagging lines and lengths that suited the field set. Pressure was created by the new-ball bowlers and as a result, Jeet Raval fell prey to Cummins who came in as first change.
Short ball on middle and leg, Taylor pulls it to deep backward square leg for a single. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 3!

Brilliant bowling from Gabriel! He has been really impressive with his bouncers. Hits the deck hard and gets it to seam in prodigiously. Taylor sways away and evades it. That was bowled at 143 clicks.
Half volley outside off, Taylor absolutely nails the drive but finds the man at extra cover.
Around the hips, tucked off the back foot to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Bouncer this time, Kane ducks under it.
Short delivery on middle and leg, half pulled to the mid-wicket region to rotate strike.
It is already time for Lunch but the umpire hasn't signaled for it. Don't know why.
Poor fielding! Taylor eases it besides the pitch on the leg side. The fielder from short mid-wicket dives to his left but makes a mess of it. A run taken.
Uses his feet to this one and buries it into the track.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The batsman plays a sweep shot. Two runs added to the total. That brings up the 50-run stand. Good going from New Zealand.
Hangs back to the loopy delivery and stonewalls it.
Nicely done. Kneels and paddle sweeps it towards fine leg for a brace.
Leg bye! Down the leg side, Taylor tries to clip it through but misses. The ball brushes the thigh pad and rolls to fine leg. A single taken.
Hangs back to the shortish delivery and blocks it.
No ball! Gabriel oversteps yet again in search of that extra mile. Back of a length around the hips, tucked around the corner for a single.
Brute of a delivery! Credit to Gabriel for steaming in and giving it his all. Sharp bouncer on off, seaming in. Taylor has to sway away from the line of the delivery in a jiffy to evade it.
Another short delivery but this one is outside off, comfortably ducked under.
Finally a good delivery after quite some time. Gabriel steams in and hits the deck hard around off. Taylor arches back, drops his wrists and leaves it with good technique.
Angling into Taylor, he covers the inswing and defends it solidly.
Spinning into Kane who lunges forward in defense.
Hangs back to the flatter delivery and punches it to covers.
Prods forward to the tossed up delivery and blocks it.
Short delivery, cut through point for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Hangs back to the shorter delivery and tucks it to mid-wicket.
Brathwaite is back on.

FOUR! 26th Test fifty for Kane Williamson! An innings of top quality. He was slow to start with but is flowing now. Typical Williamson shot. He shuffles across to the length delivery and tucks it through backward square leg. No protection in the deep and the ball rolls to the fence. The lead moves to 237.

FOUR! Beautiful! Full length ball around off, Williamson strokes it past the bowler and towards mid off. He takes off but Taylor doesn't move an inch. He knew that mid off was standing wide and the ball whistles away to the fence.
Streaky! Full length ball outside off, Taylor again goes for a booming drive but outside edges it past the diving fielder at gully who got a hand to it. A run taken.
Brilliant looking shot but for no runs! Overpitched outside off, Taylor drills it towards wide deepish mid off where Cummins get low to his left to save it.

Good bowling! He angles this one in appreciably from a length around off. Taylor shuffles and keeps it out besides the pitch on the leg side. If he missed that, he would have been a candidate for an LBW.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Taylor points his bat skywards and makes a good leave.
Shannon Gabriel returns for a bowl.

FOUR! Timing and grace written all over that stroke! Half volley outside off, Williamson leans into it and caresses it through extra cover for a majestic boundary. Held his pose after playing it, sheer quality.
Fractionally overpitched, patted back to the bowler.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Short and a lot of width on offer, Williamson is not going to miss out and flays it behind point. Chase standing near the ropes chases it to his left, slides but only comes second best in the chase.
Shaping in on a fuller length at gentle military pace, Williamson prods forward and plays it with soft hands.
Shortish in length once again, pulled to deep mid-wicket to rotate strike.
Back of a length delivery, sits up nicely for Taylor. He pulls it nicely to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Overpitched around off, driven crisply to mid off.

Almost chopped that back! Poor shot selection from Taylor. Shortish delivery, angling in and too close to cut. The batsman goes for the slash but gets a bottom edge that just goes past the off stump. He departed in the first innings attempting the same shot, needs to be careful.
Back of a length delivery, Taylor camps back and defends it stoutly.
Third no ball of the innings for the Windies! Coming in with the angle, tucked to the mid-wicket region.
Similar length delivery, pushed back to the bowler.
The umpires check for the shape of the ball but it is fine to continue.
Fuller in length, angling in, blocked watchfully.
Miguel Cummins is back on.
Shuffles to the good length delivery and turns it smartly through mid-wicket. Ambris moves to his left and keeps it to a brace.
In the channel outside off, Williamson lets it go.
Outside off, pushed of the front foot to covers.

A chirpy shout for a caught behind denied! Length delivery going down the leg side, Williamson tries to flick it but seems to have missed it by a country mile. However, Dowrich collects it and goes up in an appeal. Watching him, his teammates join in. The umpire is not interested. Brathwaite has a chat with the keeper but doesn't go for the review. The Snicko shows a spike, not sure why. There was clear daylight between bat and ball.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Reifer comes from around the wicket and bowls a fuller length ball on off. Williamson keeps his bat and pad together and offers a watertight defense.
Waits for this one and places it past point for a run.
Roach continues with the same length. Williamson has no issue in dealing with it from within the crease.
Hangs back to the short of a length delivery and stonewalls it.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

FOUR! Suddenly, the Windies have become lackluster! A few misfields and the bowling has turned out to be off color as well. Short and asking to be hit, Williamson arches back and crashes it behind point to find the ropes.
Roach goes wider of the crease and angles in a length delivery to Williamson who prods forward to dead bat it.
Outside off, left alone.
Played to the deep point region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Short and room on offer, Williamson cuts it towards Chase at backward point who doesn't stop it cleanly. Ambris hares after it from gully and keeps it down to a couple.
Hangs back to the good length delivery and blocks it nicely.
Taylor drives it hard to mid off to rotate strike.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Straying on the pads, Williamson tucks it off his hips past the keeper to the fine leg fence. 12 from the over, runs are starting to flow for the hosts.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single. 50 up for New Zealand.
Short ball, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman plays the square cut. One run added to the total. The lead also touches 200.
Another misfield! Williamson dabs it towards gully where Roston Chase gets across to his left but fumbles. Hope cuts it off and keeps the batsmen to a single.

FOUR! Shoddy stuff! Around the hips, Williamson tucks it nicely through square leg. Cummins in the deep jogs across to his left, puts in a lazy effort and makes a mess of it to concede a boundary. How poor has the fielding been in the last two overs from the Windies!
Ross Taylor comes out to bat. Meanwhile, there is a bowling change. Kemar Roach comes back for a bowl.

OUT! 2nd Test wicket for Raymon Reifer! New Zealand waste a review. Fullish delivery on off, swinging in substantially. Latham falls over a bit in an attempt to flick it across and misses to get pinged on the pads. The Windies roar in an appeal and the umpire decides to rule it out after a thought. Latham walks across to his skipper, has a chat with him and opts for the DRS. Time for the replays. There is nothing on the Snicko. The Hawk Eye rolls in. Is it going down leg? No, it is hitting the leg stump. Tom is on his way back. Reifer is absolutely pumped up. In the first innings, he had caught Henry Nicholls off guard with a similar delivery. New Zealand lead by 194.
Latham has been adjudged LBW but he has opted for the review after having a conversation with his partner. Looks adjacent to the naked eye.
Driven hard to short cover where Chase makes a good stop.
Full ball outside off, Kane strokes it towards wide mid off. Cummins dives to his left and makes a partial stop to parry it behind. A run taken.

FOUR! School boy error from Ambris! You cannot expect such a dull effort at this level of cricket, simply unacceptable. Short and room on offer, Williamson pounces on it and flays it towards backward point. Ambris ambles across to his left and lets it go through for a boundary.
Similar delivery, Williamson is in no mood to flirt with it.
Fuller in length around off, moving away with the arm. Williamson plants his front foot across to allow it through.
Change of ends for Raymon Reifer.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Drifting in towards Latham. He prods forward to defend but gets it off the inner half through backward square leg. Roach runs in from the deep to keep it down to a single.
Slow through the air, defended solidly off the front foot.
Sits deep in the crease and tucks it around the corner to rotate strike.
Similar length ball on off, Williamson punches it towards short mid-wicket where the fielder dives to his right to make a good stop.
Starts off with a loosener outside off. Short and spinning away, Latham rocks back and cuts it to sweeper cover for a run.

DRINKS BREAK. Quiet passage of play. Windies have not given much away and conceded just around 2 runs an over. This second wicket partnership is just starting to get a little bit busy with the rotation of strike. The Windies need to continue with their discipline and try and bowl the Kiwis out before 150 to stake a claim in this match. Meanwhile, Kraigg Brathwaite to roll his arm over now.
A bouncer from around the wicket, Kane ducks.
Around off, pushed towards mid on.
A length ball, Williamson just works it through mid-wicket and runs briskly to come back for the second.
Outside off, punched through covers for a quick single. Moves to 20 now and so does the partnership.

FOUR! 'Catch' is the call but it is a boundary. A short ball around middle, angling away, Latham gets on top of the bounce and pulls it through square leg. There is a man in the deep but he is more at mid-wicket. The lead moves to 182.
A bouncer, around leg, Latham ducks.
A leg slip in place for Latham.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball - but fails.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Outside off, blocked with a dead bat towards gully.
A length ball now, angling away, KW is not interested in playing at that.
Fuller again, not as wide as the previous one and Kane watches it go.
Full and wide outside off, Williamson gets to the pitch of the ball and unfurls a lovely cover drive, only to be blocked.
Gabriel is back on the field.
On middle and leg, worked straight to square leg again.
A length ball now, tucked straight to square leg.
Around off, solidly defended.
Very full and around off, pushed straight to mid off.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Looks okay to continue, Brathwaite. Roach has a word with him and a couple of concerned fielders surround them. All okay now.

Has Kraigg Brathwaite hurt himself? Seems so. Full and outside off, Williamson comes forward and drives it down the ground. Brathwaite gives it a chase from mid off and gets to the ball near the long off fence but while picking it up, he slips awkwardly. He does not move for a second, then stretches his left shoulder. Just overarms a weak throw with the right hand and it does not go far. Seeing that, the batsmen take the third.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Full and outside off, no swing, no movement, gentle medium pace, 121.3 kph to be precise, Tom prefers not to play at that.
Outside off, left alone.
Full on middle, pushed straight to mid on.
This time he gets it through. Short again, punched through point where the fielder dives but the ball goes beneath his hands. It stops near the fence and the batsmen take two.
Short and outside off, punched through point where the fielder dives to his left to stop the ball.
RAYMON REIFER to have a go as well.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
This time he gets right behind the line of the ball and defends.

NEARLY CHOPS IT BACK ON! Cummins is making the ball talk. Which makes us wonder why isn't he given the new ball. He lands this outside off on a length which puts Williamson in two minds - should I play or leave? He first decides to play, then wants to leave it. Is late and gets a bottom edge which just goes past the off stump!
Gabriel is going off the field now. Suspect for a change of shoes. Does not look that serious.
Very full on middle and off, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, driven straight to short extra cover.

Some issues for Gabriel. He is on his haunches, holding his toe. Full on middle and leg, Latham clips this through mid-wicket and takes a couple. Wants the third but is sent back. Might be some issue with Gabriel's boots. He is continuing for one more ball.
A bouncer, around leg and outside, ducked under.
Full and outside off, over-compensation and Tom is ready for it. Leans and drives the ball through the covers for a couple. Moves to 11 and takes the lead to 171.

FOUR! A rare bad ball as far as the plan is concerned. The field is set such that the line has to be around off and middle. There is no fine leg and he is placed at deep square leg instead. So, once the ball is on the pads, it is easy pickings for Latham who just flicks it to the fine leg fence.
A short ball, on middle and leg, Latham trusts the bounce and shoulders arms, allowing the ball to go over the sticks.
The skipper is away. A short ball, around middle, pulled through mid-wicket for a brace.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
A bouncer now, Kane ducks.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
A length ball, right in line of the stumps, Williamson defends watchfully.
KANE WILLIAMSON walks in at number 3, replacing Raval.

OUT! Caught and bowled! Cummins revels in the pressure created by the new-ball bowlers. New Zealand were not given much freebies by Roach and Gabriel, hence, at the first instance they spot a change, they think now is the time to score. The ball is not that short but Raval thinks it is there to be pulled. That error in judgement costs him as he miscues it back to the bowler. Never easy to take return catches, especially if you are a fast bowler and Cummins does really well to take that chance. NEW ZEALAND ARE EFFECTIVELY 163/1.
MIGUEL CUMMINS is given the ball now as Roach takes a break.
A fuller ball on middle, punched back to the bowler.
A short ball down the leg side, played straight to square leg.
Full and outside off, TL looks to drive but finds mid off.

NO BALL. Number 2 for Gabriel and also for the Windies. He has overstepped by an even bigger margin than the previous one. The ball is pretty decent, full and outside off, Tom looks to guide it to third man but misses.
Similar length to the previous one, Latham taps it towards cover.
Holds the length back a touch, in line of the stumps, Latham trusts the bounce and lets it go.
On a length, around middle, defended solidly.
Nice discipline, full and just around off, going away, Raval watches it go.
One more leave outside off.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
A length ball around middle and leg, defended solidly.
On the pads, clipped through mid-wicket for a couple.
Landed outside off, let through.
A length ball outside off, good bounce, Latham looks to push at that but misses.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Outside off, left alone.

NO BALL. First one of the innings. Strives for extra pace, bowling 149.6 kph, but oversteps by a fairly large margin. Latham looks to push at that away from his body and gets beaten. The lead is now 160.
A short ball, aimed at the batsman's face, Raval plays it a bit uncomfortably to the leg side for a single.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Landed on a length outside off, let through to the keeper.

FOUR! That breaks the shackles a little bit and gives me something different to write. Roach swerves from his consistency and bangs it in short. But it barely comes at chest height to Latham who comfortably pulls it through mid-wicket for the first boundary of the innings.
One more time. The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Good lines, nice consistency, hitting the good length part, keeping it just outside off and then using the angle. Left alone again.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump again.
Full and outside off, left alone again.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
A length ball around middle and leg, Latham looks to defend but gets an inside edge through square leg. A single taken.
A length ball outside off, angling away, left alone.
Make that a hat-trick of leaves.
One more leave outside off.
Outside off, let through to the keeper.
Down the leg side, Jeet misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Meanwhile, it has started to drizzle. Clouds were forming a group and there is a rain threat anyway. Hopefully, this passes over.
A length ball, around leg and middle, Raval defends this watchfully.
KEMAR ROACH to share the new ball.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
A length ball, around middle and leg, watchfully defended.
First run of the innings. Pushes this towards cover and takes the single.
Gets right behind the line of this one and defends it towards point.
Outside off, left alone.
Very full wide outside off, Raval looks to steer it to third man but misses.
